name: Opus Value
strategy: A trend book that follows what is working on the tape: long energy, gold miners and quality, momentum cut to a starter size after semis leadership broke, and smaller shorts in long-duration Treasuries and consumer discretionary, with 23% in cash.
reassessment_note: The 10-14 to 10-16 selloff was led by semiconductors, and stops fired across the field on TSM, AMD, AMAT, LRCX, MU, SOXL and TQQQ. That is the leadership MTUM is built around: its six- and twelve-month ranking left it loaded with AI and chip winners, and it fell about 7% in a week the last time that trade reversed (July). MTUM is now -9.3% on this leg, 3 points from its -12% stop, and it is the main reason this book is -5.55%. A trend book should not keep its largest weight in a factor whose leading component just broke trend, so I am cutting MTUM from 26% to 12% rather than riding it into the stop. The TLT short is -3.8% because bonds caught a risk-off bid, so I am trimming it from 17% to 12% under a tighter stop and keeping the thesis but less of the risk. The winning legs, XLE (+7.6%), and the defensive factor QUAL are kept or increased. The freed weight goes to cash at 4% APY instead of a new bet. Research limits: web search returned no usable coverage of this week's tape, Treasury yields or oil, so the semis read comes from the desk's list of stops that fired and the momentum read comes from earlier 2026 coverage of MTUM's chip concentration. Because the book re-enters at the 10-19 close, every stop and take-profit below is measured from the new fill. Novelty check: no symbol in this book appears in the Round 2 book (UNH, CI, XOM, ACN, GLD, CVX, ADBE, ETH-USD), so the same-direction overlap is 0%.

positions.thesis: Energy is the strongest trend in this book: +7.6% on the leg, and it held up through the chip selloff because the oil-driven stagflation regime has not reversed. Increased from 14% to 16% to follow the trend that is working. A 10% stop from the new fill protects most of the gain if oil breaks.

Gold miners give leveraged exposure to the inflation and stagflation hedge, and they are flat on the leg despite a volatile week (GDX stops fired elsewhere on 10-14). Size stays at 15%. The 15% stop is wide because miners are volatile, and a 35% take-profit locks in a gold blow-off.

Quality has been flat (-0.4%) while momentum fell 9%. That is the defensive factor doing its job in a growth unwind, so it moves up from 12% to 14% and becomes the book's main equity-factor exposure in place of MTUM.

Cut from 26% to 12%. MTUM holds a lot of the AI and semiconductor leaders whose stops fired 10-14 to 10-16. I keep a starter position in case the broader momentum trend resumes after the shakeout, but under a tight 8% stop from the new fill, because a trend book should not add to a factor that just broke trend.

Long-end yields remain near multi-decade highs (the 10-year was about 5% in late September) and sticky inflation argues for a term premium. But the leg is -3.8% because bonds caught a risk-off bid during the selloff. I trim from 17% to 12% under a 6% stop from the new fill, which caps the damage if the flight to safety continues.

Consumer discretionary is the weakest fundamental trend after a weak payroll print and an energy-price squeeze on household budgets. It is only -1.9% against the book, so the 8% size stays and the stop is tightened to 8% from the new fill.
